A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization and the expanded title in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic simulations, MNIST/FashionMNIST experiments, and two-layer neural-network experiments, including Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds linear-regression validation and deep-network experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

M1.justification: The linear and random-feature ridge/minimum-norm estimators and norm-based capacity framework are unchanged. The added deep architectures serve as empirical validation of the existing framework.

E1.justification: Appendix H.4 adds CIFAR-10 classification with noisy training labels, extending coverage to natural images. Synthetic data, MNIST, and FashionMNIST coverage is retained; additional architectures on MNIST do not themselves constitute new task coverage.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons with parameter count, degrees of freedom, Frobenius norm/distance, spectral complexity, and path norm are retained. The new deep-network experiments reuse the parameter-count/path-norm comparison without introducing a new competing capacity measure.

E3.justification: H.4 introduces deep-model width/channel sweeps, including an MLP/CNN protocol with a 4,000/12,000 MNIST split, 15% symmetric training-label noise, cross-entropy training, and SGD for up to 500 epochs. It also adds a separate CIFAR-10/ResNet18 evaluation. New Figure 4 evaluates linear regression at lambda = 0.005; existing H.3 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: H.4 substantially extends the analysis of whether norm-based learning-curve patterns persist beyond two-layer networks, using three-layer MLPs, CNNs, and ResNet18. New D.3.1/Figure 4 also examines linear-regression bias and variance across parameterization regimes. Existing activation-function and label-noise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten repetitions per hidden-layer dimension and mean/standard-deviation curves for H.3. The added H.4 experiments introduce no stated repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds linear-regression bias/variance results in Figure 4 and deep-network error, width/channel, and path-norm curves in Figures 23–25. The new deep-network findings report joint decreases in risk and norm under sufficient over-parameterization. Existing plotted results are retained; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2's separately stated simplified power-law concentration guarantee in Theorem 3.4 is omitted. v3 retains the full non-asymptotic bound in Theorem D.6, while the principal deterministic-equivalent formulas, risk–norm relationships, and corresponding appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims about norm-based capacity, phase transitions, the absence of double descent under that capacity view, and nonmonotone norm-based scaling laws. The phi-curve terminology already appears in v2; the new experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: H.4 newly interprets deep-network results as suggesting that double descent is transient while phase transitions and phi-shaped behavior are more fundamental. D.3.1 adds interpretations of linear-regression bias–variance behavior. The data-assumption caveat highlighted in v3's introduction was already discussed in v2's G.1.

D1.justification: H.4 adds MLP/CNN architecture, preprocessing, split, noise-generation, optimizer, and training-budget details. v3 also expands its reported resource availability from representative-figure code to replication materials, scripts with pinned versions, and trained models.

R1.justification: v3 adds the ResNet reference by He et al. and the CIFAR reference by Krizhevsky et al. It connects the new ResNet18 experiments to a reproduction of the already-cited deep double-descent study. The broader related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative is reorganized around RFMs: linear-regression preliminaries and results move into Appendices B and D, and former Section 4 becomes separate Sections 3 and 4. Appendix D integrates statements, proofs, and discussion. The title, author information, and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the NeurIPS layout with changed typography, title/author presentation, and extensive reflow. It relocates the linear-regression summary table and risk–norm figure, adds Figures 4 and 23–25, and corrects the first panel of the RFM path-norm figure to display risk versus parameter count.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful additional evidence beyond shallow models, especially the CIFAR-10/ResNet18 experiment, and expands reproduction information while preserving the main theoretical development and existing results. The gain is limited by the qualitative nature of the new validation, unspecified repeated-run uncertainty, and sparse ResNet18 protocol details in the PDF.
